The foundational lens is built upon the sample characterization (N=157) and group classification (N=103 vs N=54), enabling a controlled experimental design. Variance heterogeneity among variables (8 out of 13) necessitates robust statistical inference techniques such as Welch's t-test, which accounts for unequal variances. The T-test reveals only four significant differences, indicating that while some traits differ significantly, others remain invariant across continents. This suggests that performance metrics are not uniformly distributed but rather exhibit selective divergence. The derived primitives form a mathematical foundation for probabilistic reasoning in GSI and dynamic state transitions in GSE. The failure mode lies in assuming uniformity across all variables, which is mitigated by variance heterogeneity detection. Dualities emerge in the contrast between variance structure and significance outcomes, reflecting the complexity of multi-dimensional athletic performance.
